messages:
rachel-customer: Hey team — past 24h we've seen a lot of our calls spike in p50/p95 and sometimes 502s. Our traces show the first attempt goes to us-east, then the SDK retries and hits eu-west, which makes latency huge and we got charged for multiple attempts. Can we get help?

maria-support: Sorry you're seeing that, rachel. Can you share the SDK version and the exact retry config? Also any request IDs or a short trace would help.

rachel-customer: SDK v1.4.2. We use the default client; don't set a region explicitly. Example trace IDs: trace=tr-8fb3 and trace=tr-8fb7. Attached logs show: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z request_id=tr-8fb3 target=us-east status=502 latency=310ms
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z client: retrying attempt=2 fallback_region=eu-west
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z request_id=tr-8fb3 target=eu-west status=200 latency=5200ms
```
We only saw this after a customer-facing deploy but can't repro locally yet.

lee-sdk: Thanks — that log looks like hedged/parallel retries + fallback routing. v1.4.2 changed the default hedging window (went from 120ms to 40ms) and also enabled regional fallthrough for latency SLOs. If the initial region returns a 5xx quickly we might spin up a hedged request to the next region. That can cause expensive double-tokens and cross-region latencies if the fallback region is far.

maria-support: Two tracks: (1) short-term mitigation for rachel: set env REDWOOD_SDK_HEDGING_ENABLED=false or set hedging_window_ms=250 to reduce parallel attempts; and (2) longer-term we'll investigate routing policy and whether a 502 should trigger immediate cross-region hedge.

devon-telemetry: FYI I pulled the tenant's routing history. Notable: at 14:02 we saw an upstream NLB returning 502 from us-east for ~1.5s and then us-east recovered. The SDK's hedged attempt to eu-west completed but with large RTT. I can attach the slice.

rachel-customer: OK we'll try disabling hedging now. Quick Q: will turning hedging off stop retries entirely? We still want simple backoff, just no cross-region hedges.

lee-sdk: Correct — hedging=false keeps normal retry/backoff behavior (sequential retries to same region according to the configured fallback order). Example config snippet you can add: 
```
client = RedwoodClient(
  region="auto",
  hedging_enabled=False,
  retry_policy={"max_attempts":3, "backoff_ms":200}
)
```
That keeps retries in-region unless the server returns explicit X-Fallback-Allowed header.

maria-support: rachel, could you also send one full request/response payload (sanitized) and the SDK debug logs (set REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=debug) for the time window? Helps us confirm whether retries were hedged or sequential.

rachel-customer: Sending logs in a sec. Also saw a customer billing spike — charged twice for some requests because both attempts consumed tokens. Is that expected?

lee-sdk: Yes, each served token is billable. We have a billing guard for obvious double-charges in extreme incidents but hedged requests that both produce output are billable. We can open a billing investigation if you want a partial credit for that window.

maria-support: We'll open a ticket with billing. For engineering: @lee-sdk and @devon-telemetry — can you validate whether a transient 502 should have produced an immediate cross-region hedge with our routing policy? If yes, we should add a short circuit: if 5xx latency >200ms, prefer local recovery instead of cross-region.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-4821 for increased hedged cross-region traffic — assigned to eng-runtime.

lee-sdk: Will investigate. My hypothesis: combination of reduced hedging window + fallback order shuffle caused the client to consider eu-west lower latency historically and immediately spin a hedged request. I'll run a sim with tenant routing weights and the v1.4.2 defaults.

devon-telemetry: I'll pull per-tenant model of recent latency distributions and check whether regional preference drifted. If we confirm a router/telemetry churn bug we can patch a config flag to prefer same-region retries for 5xx within a short TTL.

rachel-customer: Thanks team — happy to apply the hedging=false workaround for now. Please keep me posted, and we'd appreciate a billing review. :pray:

maria-support: Got it. We'll confirm once devs have a root cause. In the meantime, note for others: disable hedging or bump hedging_window_ms if you see cross-region cost/latency spikes after upgrades. :point_up:
